So first of all, vulnerabilities exist for a couple reasons.

Let us just take out the vulnerabilities that require the user be explicitly involved. From a strictly programmatic perspective, these aren't vulnerabilities: merely features. Almost everyone in the security sphere agrees that the person who has admin access to a machine should be allowed to, if they want, blow it up. This isn't a fault, it is a feature.

So what about all those other vulnerabilities that exist? Many of these (more modern) vulnerabilities exist because of the interaction between different parts in ways that weren't analyzed. It is really difficult to exhaustively test all possible interactions. It is also really difficult to write an OS with completely verifiable code.

Vulnerabilities exist because, if they tried to to actually guarantee zero vulnerabilities on release, they would never release the damn stuff. This is why we have patches. This is also why we have vulnerabilities, because it is economically infeasible to take them all out before hand.

Bundesliga Matchday 21

Date: Friday, 13 February, 2015

Venue: Westfalenstadion, Dortmund

Time: 2:30 EST, 19:30 GMT, 20:30 CET

Match Official: Tobias Spieler

KEY PLAYERS

BVB: Marco Reus

Mainz: Shinji Okazaki

INJURIES

BVB: Großkreutz, Kehl, Durm, Bender & Blaszczyowski.

Mainz: Karius, Moritz, Nedelev & Jairo.

POSSIBLE LINEUPS

BVB: Weidenfeller(GK), Piszczek(RB), Subotic(CB), Hummels(CB), Schmelzer(LB), Gündogan(CM), Sahin(CM), Kagawa(CAM), Kampl(LAM), Reus(RAM), and Aubameyang(ST).

Mainz: Kapino(GK), Brosinski(RB), Bell(CB), Bungert(CB), Bengtsson(LB), Baumgartlinger(CM), Geis(CM), Malli(CAM), Hofmann(LAM), Clemens(RAM), and Okazaki(ST).

MATCH FACTS

  • Only 3 points stand between 16th-placed Dortmund and 13th-placed Mainz 05

  • Borussia Dortmund are undefeated in their last 9 home matches against Mainz in all competitions.

  • Mainz 05 are winless in 8 away matches.

  • Dortmund's decline began with the first-leg 2-0 loss to Mainz 05.

  • Mainz 05 are yet to record an away win in Dortmund in the B'Liga( 4 draws, 4 losses)

  • Dortmund haven't lost a home match on a Friday evening in 11 years. ( Last lost 0-1 on 30 January, 2004 against Schalke).

  • Thanks to their 2-0 home win in the meeting earlier this season, Mainz ended a run of six straight defeats and eight games without a win against Dortmund (D1, L7).

  • Dortmund’s 3-0 win in Freiburg was their first victory since early December (1-0 against Hoffenheim). They now need to improve their home form: BVB have lost more matches on home soil (4) than they’ve won (3) this season.

  • The 05ers have lost only six of their first 20 league games this season, a new club record. However, they have also won just four – the only time they have recorded fewer wins at this stage was in their 2006/07 relegation campaign (3). FSV have drawn the most games in the league (10).

  • BVB have collected just 19 points from their first 20 league fixtures in 2014/15. They have only had fewer points at this stage in 1971/72 (15, converted to the 3-points-per-win system), a season that ended in relegation, and in 1984/85 (17 when converted).

  • Mainz have won just one of their last 12 BL games (5-0 against Paderborn on matchday 18) and are without an away victory since their 3-1 win in Berlin on matchday 3 (D5, L3). The last time FSV waited longer for three points on the road was in 2011/12 (12 games).

  • Dortmund boss Jürgen Klopp made a total of 325 second-division appearances for Mainz between 1990 and 2001 (52 goals). He then managed FSV until summer 2008, leading the 05ers to the Bundesliga for the first time in 2004.

  • Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang had a hand in all three of BVB’s goals in Freiburg (2 goals + 1 assist) and has now been involved in 11 of their last 16 BL goals (7 goals + 4 assists).

  • Mainz will be without first-choice keeper Loris Karius following his red card against Hertha.

  • Lukasz Piszczek is set for his 200th BL games, while Neven Subotic could make his 175th top-flight appearance in Dortmund colours. Sebastian Kehl turns 35 on the day of the match.

  • Neven Subotic (2006-2008 at Mainz), Erik Durm (2010-2012 at Mainz) and Jonas Hofmann (currently on loan at FSV from Dortmund) all come up against their former club.
